forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, ℓ with 0 ≤ k, ℓ ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose ℓ]_q is a polynomial in q, then it has only nonnegative coefficients.

forbidden_claims.label: lem_20260329120647_c4ea7dea
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let a, b, r be integers with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0. Set I := {a+1, a+2, ..., b}, and let R := Q[x_s : s in I] be the polynomial ring graded by deg(x_s) = s for each s in I. For each positive integer d define M_d(u,v) := |{m in Z : u < m <= v and d divides m}|. Assume M_d(r+a, r+b) >= M_d(a,b) for every positive integer d. Then there exists a family (f_s)_{s in I} of homogeneous polynomials in R such that deg(f_s) = r+s for every s in I, and the ordered list of these polynomials in increasing order of s is a regular sequence in R. If I is empty, this means the empty family.

forbidden_claims.label: lem_20260329110006_654a633e
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let a, b, r, j be integers with 0 <= a <= b, r >= 0, and 0 <= j <= floor(r (b - a) / 2). Put I := {a+1, a+2, ..., b}. For each positive integer d, define M_d(u,v) := |{m in Z : u < m <= v and d divides m}|, and assume M_d(r+a,r+b) >= M_d(a,b) for every positive integer d. Let X_j be the set of pairs (S, lambda) such that S is a subset of I, lambda is a finite multiset of elements of I, |lambda| denotes the sum of the elements of lambda, and |lambda| + sum_{s in S} (r + s) = j. Then there exists an involution iota_j : X_j -> X_j such that: (1) if iota_j(S,lambda) = (S',lambda') != (S,lambda), then |S'| is congruent to |S| + 1 modulo 2; and (2) if iota_j(S,lambda) = (S,lambda), then |S| is even.

forbidden_claims.label: lem_20260329092547_6a64d34a
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: For integers a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, let q be an indeterminate, define (q;q)_n := product_{j=1}^n (1 - q^j) for n >= 0 with (q;q)_0 := 1, set R_{a,b,r}(q) := ((q;q)_{r+b} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_b), and define D := r (b - a). Assume that R_{a,b,r}(q) belongs to Z[q]. Then for every integer j with 0 <= j <= floor(D/2), the coefficient of q^j in R_{a,b,r}(q) is a nonnegative integer.

forbidden_claims.label: lem_20260329074016_d9949d95
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let a, b, r be integers with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0. Define P_{a,b,r}(q) := product_{i=a+1}^{b} ((1 - q^(r+i)) / (1 - q^i)), with empty product equal to 1. Assume that for every positive integer d one has floor((r+b)/d) - floor((r+a)/d) >= floor(b/d) - floor(a/d). Then P_{a,b,r}(q) is a polynomial in Z[q], and every coefficient of P_{a,b,r}(q) is nonnegative.

payload.statement_nl: Let A be a graded commutative Q-algebra, let phi : A -> A be a graded Q-algebra automorphism, and let u_1,...,u_n be homogeneous elements of A. Then u_1,...,u_n is a regular sequence if and only if phi(u_1),...,phi(u_n) is a regular sequence. Moreover deg(phi(u_i)) = deg(u_i) for every i.

result_payload.proof_nl: Let v_i := phi(u_i) for i = 1,...,n. For each i = 0,...,n, set I_i := (u_1,...,u_i) and J_i := (v_1,...,v_i), with I_0 = J_0 = (0). Because phi is an algebra automorphism, phi(I_i) = J_i for every i. Hence phi induces an isomorphism of quotient rings bar_phi_i : A / I_i -> A / J_i, given by a + I_i |-> phi(a) + J_i; its inverse is induced by phi^{-1}. Now let u_i have degree d. Since phi is a graded automorphism, it preserves each graded piece, so phi(u_i) also lies in the degree-d piece. Therefore deg(phi(u_i)) = d = deg(u_i) for every i. It remains to prove preservation of regular sequences. Use the standard ring-theoretic definition: a sequence x_1,...,x_n is regular if for each i >= 1, the class of x_i is a non-zero-divisor in A / (x_1,...,x_{i-1}); if one also adopts the common extra condition that the final quotient A / (x_1,...,x_n) be nonzero, that condition is also preserved here because the final quotients are isomorphic. Assume first that u_1,...,u_n is a regular sequence. Fix i with 1 <= i <= n. Suppose that in A / J_{i-1} one has (v_i + J_{i-1})(a + J_{i-1}) = 0. Then v_i a is in J_{i-1} = phi(I_{i-1}). Applying phi^{-1}, we get u_i phi^{-1}(a) in I_{i-1}. Equivalently, in A / I_{i-1} we have (u_i + I_{i-1})(phi^{-1}(a) + I_{i-1}) = 0. Since u_i + I_{i-1} is a non-zero-divisor in A / I_{i-1}, it follows that phi^{-1}(a) + I_{i-1} = 0, so phi^{-1}(a) is in I_{i-1}. Applying phi, we obtain a in J_{i-1}. Thus v_i + J_{i-1} is a non-zero-divisor in A / J_{i-1}. Since this holds for every i, the sequence v_1,...,v_n is regular. If one includes the additional condition A / I_n != 0 in the definition, it is preserved as well because bar_phi_n is an isomorphism A / I_n ~= A / J_n. Conversely, if v_1,...,v_n is regular, the same argument applied to the automorphism phi^{-1} shows that u_1,...,u_n is regular. Therefore u_1,...,u_n is a regular sequence if and only if phi(u_1),...,phi(u_n) is a regular sequence. Together with the degree argument above, this proves the lemma.
result_payload.proof_summary: An automorphism sends each initial ideal (u_1,...,u_{i-1}) to (phi(u_1),...,phi(u_{i-1})) and therefore induces isomorphisms of the corresponding quotients. Under these quotient isomorphisms, the class of u_i maps to the class of phi(u_i), so non-zero-divisorness is preserved in both directions; the optional final nonzero-quotient condition is preserved as well. Degree preservation is immediate from the definition of a graded automorphism.
